page: Microsoft Azure L4s_v4 is a virtual machine instance from the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, and it is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2158.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.48 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 3990.37 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression score of 26.74 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also a limiting factor, with large-block read-only bandwidth measured at 36.35 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 25.49 GB/sec, both falling into lower performance percentiles. Database operations on Passmark score an average 2891.14, while Redis SET operations perform weakly at 5.68 million operations per second.

The hardware profile offers a high ratio of memory to vCPUs alongside fast local NVMe storage, which provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring localized data caching without the overhead of external storage arrays. However, the low physical core count and constrained memory bandwidth present clear tradeoffs for highly parallelized compute tasks or large-scale in-memory databases. The instance is best suited for small-to-medium database workloads, low-latency local caching, single-threaded processing tasks, and basic web serving.
